::: {.content-visible when-format="docx"}
# Book_23 — OrgPath and E911 Compliance
:::


::: {.callout-note}
Every year, callers in federal office buildings dial 911 and the PSAP cannot find them. The building address is in the system — but which floor? Which conference room? Which wing of a campus with six identical towers? Kari's Law and RAY BAUM's Act §506 require that multi-line telephone systems and UCaaS platforms transmit a dispatchable location precise enough to find a person, not just a building. LocPath (ADR-102) provides the governing substrate: a structured location record with civic address and sub-address precision. The E911 compliance layer (ADR-104) tests every obligated node, routes findings by severity, and closes the gap between federal law and federal practice.
:::

## Companion canon

For the normative specifications this narrative paraphrases:

- [ADR-104 — E911 Compliance Layer](/docs/adr/adr-104-e911-compliance-layer.html) — the binding canon source for this book: dispatchable location obligations, GOV-LOCPATH-012/013/014 error codes, MLTS scope, and RTLS observational model.
- [ADR-102 — LocPath](/docs/adr/adr-102-locpath-location-addressing.html) — the physical-location addressing dimension: site/building/floor/space hierarchy, civic address schema, e911 block, and inheritance rules.
- [UIAO_194 — LocPath Specification](/docs/specs/uiao-194-locpath.html) — normative field-level specification for LocPath nodes, the Dynamic Location Context source enum, and the completeness check algorithm.
- [Architecture Decision Records](/docs/adr/index.html) — the binding record; this book is governed primarily by ADR-104 and ADR-102.
